purpose: Exact donor path/function targets for token-efficient GBA/GBC verification before bulk mining.

verified_facts: Emerald has distinct indoor and outdoor field-move presentation state machines.
Surf, Fly and Waterfall have explicit multi-step field-effect state machines.
Field-effect script table includes Surf, Fly, Strength, Waterfall, Dive, Teleport, ash, splash, sparkle and related effects.
targets.next_action: Extract concise state sequences and referenced graphics only; do not inventory all field effects yet.

verified_facts: The field-effect registry exposes a broad set of reusable environmental/action primitives.
These effects are source-addressable and can be mined by referenced sprite/palette resources instead of broad asset scanning.
targets.next_action: Trace only the highest-value primitives to graphics and timing implementations.

verified_facts: Each preview entry binds a map section, visited/world-map flag, tile graphics, tilemap and palette.
Dedicated preview art exists for many major Kanto/Sevii locations.
The system tracks whether the map was visited before.
targets.next_action: Record trigger/visited behavior and compact resource contract; no need to inspect every preview image.

verified_facts: Elite Four and Champion lighting uses ordered palette arrays plus per-step timers.
The task repeatedly loads BG palette slot 7 and reapplies the global tint.
targets.next_action: Extract timer sequences and state flow; classify as technique evidence without porting palettes.

verified_facts: The Deoxys triangle combines progress variables, step-count gating, object relocation, palette changes, sound and a field effect.
Object coordinates and palette are indexed by interaction state.
targets.next_action: Summarize the state-machine pattern as technique/novel-detail evidence; donor art is not required.

verified_facts: Dungeon monster rendering computes a status-sprite bitmask and passes it to the Pokemon sprite layer.
The status renderer has two status-sprite slots per Pokemon.
GetNextStatusSymbol cycles through active status bits.
The table maps statuses including burn, poison, confusion, taunt, shield states, curse, sure-shot, Focus Energy, sleep, stat-down and frozen to graphical families/palette variants.
targets.next_action: Trace sStatusGfxInfo and its backing graphics files, then capture one representative cycling sequence.
Map selected graphics to move/object scripts; avoid cataloging every common effect.
Sample only animations using the distinctive primitive set and record timing/layering patterns Platinum does not already exploit.

verified_facts: Ruby exposes the same broad source families as Emerald for battle animations, field effects and animated tiles.
Mining should begin with structural/resource deltas against Emerald, not an independent broad pass.
targets.next_action: Compute targeted file/resource deltas for high-value subsystems before any manual inspection.
Inspect only unique Pikachu presentation states and unusually clear battle-transition/effect ideas; high rejection threshold.
